messages:
From: Mike Hernandez <mike@retailnova.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API capacity uplift — initial ask

Evelyn,

Thanks for the quick sync last week. We're seeing sustained growth in our query volume and want to formalize an uplift to our hosted API commit starting July 1. High-level ask:

- Current monthly commit: 1.2B tokens
- Target monthly commit: 2.0B tokens (phased: 1.6B in July, 2.0B in August)
- Preferred ratebands: keep current per-token pricing if possible; open to small step-up in rates if we get a tighter latency SLA

I've attached our May usage export for context. Next steps from our side: procurement will need a SOW + final pricing to issue a PO. Can you put together a proposal with two options (conservative and aggressive uplift) and any recommended soft-throttle guardrails?

Thanks,
Mike Hernandez
Sr. Product Ops | RetailNova
attachments: usage_report_May2026.csv
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Mike Hernandez <mike@retailnova.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API capacity uplift — initial ask

Hi Mike — really appreciate the detail. We can support the uplift and I sketched two options below. I've attached a draft SOW (RetailNova_SOW_v2.pdf) so procurement has something to review quickly.

Option A — Conservative
- Phase: 1.6B (Jul), 2.0B (Aug)
- Rateband: current hosted per-token price + 6% uplift
- Burst pocket: +15% monthly for spikes
- SLA: standard latency SLO (p95 < 300ms)

Option B — Aggressive (recommended for high-throughput storefronts)
- Phase: immediate 2.0B commit
- Rateband: current price + 12% (volume discount kicks in at 2.5B)
- Burst pocket: +25% monthly, with automatic soft-throttle when sustained above 110%
- SLA: enhanced latency SLO (p95 < 220ms) with a small credit for sustained miss

Questions for you:
1) Do you need dedicated capacity (Reserved/Dedicated) or is hosted with guaranteed commit sufficient?
2) Invoice cadence preference: monthly or quarterly?
3) Any required PO/contract terms procurement insists on (net-30, PO routing)?

I'll loop in Karthik and Vanessa to get pricing and provisioning timelines. If this looks reasonable, we'll finalize the SOW and send for signature.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Team — quick internal note after Mike's ask and my reply. Context excerpted from Mike: "target monthly commit: 2.0B tokens (phased: 1.6B in July, 2.0B in August)".

Recommendation (single-path to move fast):
- Approve Option A as base for procurement (conservative, phased).
- Offer Option B as a one-time accelerated upgrade with a 10% implementation credit if they sign within 7 business days.

Action items:
- Ben: confirm billing cadence impact and draft invoice language for monthly net-30 vs quarterly prepay. Also model revenue recognition timing for phased uplift.
- Karthik: confirm whether we can meet p95 < 220ms on hosted for the aggressive option or if we should propose Dedicated pools for that SLA. Provide ETA to enable enhanced latency.
- Marissa: provisioning timeline — what's the earliest we can scale their hosted pool and how to order burst capacity? Include runbook for soft-throttle triggers.
- Vanessa: review SOW language; tighten the SLA credit wording to be explicit (thresholds / credit calc).

I'll hold on final SOW changes until we have pricing and provisioning windows.

Thanks,
Evelyn
